no-restricted-syntax.message: for..in loops iterate over the entire prototype chain, which is virtually never what you want. Use Object.{keys,values,entries}, and iterate over the resulting array.
iterators/generators require regenerator-runtime, which is too heavyweight for this guide to allow them. Separately, loops should be avoided in favor of array iterations.
Labels are a form of GOTO; using them makes code confusing and hard to maintain and understand.
`with` is disallowed in strict mode because it makes code impossible to predict and optimize.

patterns.message: Do not import directly from MV2/MV3 implementations. Use the appropriate alias or index file instead.

rules.message: Do not import directly from src/. Use specific submodules like src/utils instead.

clauses.text: **Primitives**: When you access a primitive type you work directly on its value.
clauses.reason: Educational semantics; supported browser targets must be selected by the consumer.

clauses.text: **Complex**: When you access a complex type you work on a reference to its value.
clauses.reason: Educational explanation of reference values.

clauses.text: Use `const` for all of your references; avoid using `var`. eslint: [`prefer-const`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/prefer-const), [`no-const-assign`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-const-assign)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: If you must reassign references, use `let` instead of `var`. eslint: [`no-var`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-var)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Note that both `let` and `const` are block-scoped, whereas `var` is function-scoped.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Only quote properties that are invalid identifiers. eslint: [`quote-props`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/quote-props)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Do not call `Object.prototype` methods directly, such as `hasOwnProperty`, `propertyIsEnumerable`, and `isPrototypeOf`. eslint: [`no-prototype-builtins`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-prototype-builtins)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Prefer the object spread syntax over [`Object.assign`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/assign) to shallow-copy objects. Use the object rest parameter syntax to get a new object with certain properties omitted. eslint: [`prefer-object-spread`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/prefer-object-spread)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use array spreads `...` to copy arrays.
clauses.reason: Recognizing arbitrary copying algorithms requires semantic intent; reviewed manually.

clauses.text: To convert an iterable object to an array, use spreads `...` instead of [`Array.from`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/from)
clauses.reason: An unknown JavaScript value may be array-like rather than iterable; no speculative rewrite.

clauses.text: Use [`Array.from`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/from) for converting an array-like object to an array.
clauses.reason: Whether an arbitrary runtime value is array-like requires runtime information.

clauses.text: Use [`Array.from`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/from) instead of spread `...` for mapping over iterables, because it avoids creating an intermediate array.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use return statements in array method callbacks. It’s ok to omit the return if the function body consists of a single statement returning an expression without side effects. eslint: [`array-callback-return`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/array-callback-return)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use object destructuring when accessing and using multiple properties of an object. eslint: [`prefer-destructuring`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/prefer-destructuring)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use array destructuring. eslint: [`prefer-destructuring`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/prefer-destructuring)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use object destructuring for multiple return values, not array destructuring.
clauses.reason: Distinguishing multiple return values from an intentional array API requires review.

clauses.text: Use single quotes `''` for strings. eslint: [`quotes`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/quotes)

clauses.text: Strings that cause the line to go over 120 characters should not be written across multiple lines using string concatenation.
clauses.reason: Sample precedence: max-len, no-useless-concat retains its inherited/explicit options and severity.

clauses.text: When programmatically building up strings, use template strings instead of concatenation. eslint: [`prefer-template`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/prefer-template) [`template-curly-spacing`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/template-curly-spacing)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Never use `eval()` on a string, it opens too many vulnerabilities. eslint: [`no-eval`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-eval)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Do not unnecessarily escape characters in strings. eslint: [`no-useless-escape`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-useless-escape)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Wrap immediately invoked function expressions in parentheses. eslint: [`wrap-iife`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/wrap-iife)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Never declare a function in a non-function block (`if`, `while`, etc). Assign the function to a variable instead. Browsers will allow you to do it, but they all interpret it differently, which is bad news bears. eslint: [`no-loop-func`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-loop-func)

clauses.text: Never name a parameter `arguments`. This will take precedence over the `arguments` object that is given to every function scope.

clauses.text: Never use `arguments`, opt to use rest syntax `...` instead. eslint: [`prefer-rest-params`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/prefer-rest-params)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use default parameter syntax rather than mutating function arguments.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Avoid side effects with default parameters.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Always put default parameters last. eslint: [`default-param-last`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/default-param-last)

clauses.text: Never use the Function constructor to create a new function. eslint: [`no-new-func`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-new-func)

clauses.text: Spacing in a function signature. eslint: [`space-before-function-paren`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/space-before-function-paren) [`space-before-blocks`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/space-before-blocks)

clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Never reassign parameters. eslint: [`no-param-reassign`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-param-reassign)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Prefer the use of the spread syntax `...` to call variadic functions. eslint: [`prefer-spread`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/prefer-spread)

clauses.text: Functions with multiline signatures, or invocations, should be indented just like every other multiline list in this guide: with each item on a line by itself, with a trailing comma on the last item. eslint: [`function-paren-newline`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/function-paren-newline)

clauses.text: When you must use an anonymous function (as when passing an inline callback), use arrow function notation. eslint: [`prefer-arrow-callback`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/prefer-arrow-callback), [`arrow-spacing`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/arrow-spacing)

clauses.text: Always include parentheses around arguments for clarity and consistency. eslint: [`arrow-parens`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/arrow-parens)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Enforce the location of arrow function bodies with implicit returns. eslint: [`implicit-arrow-linebreak`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/implicit-arrow-linebreak)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Always use `class`. Avoid manipulating `prototype` directly.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Methods can return `this` to help with method chaining.
clauses.reason: Method chaining is optional API design guidance.

clauses.text: Classes have a default constructor if one is not specified. An empty constructor function or one that just delegates to a parent class is unnecessary. eslint: [`no-useless-constructor`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-useless-constructor)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Class methods should use `this` or be made into a static method unless an external library or framework requires using specific non-static methods. Being an instance method should indicate that it behaves differently based on properties of the receiver. eslint: [`class-methods-use-this`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/class-methods-use-this)

clauses.text: Always use modules (`import`/`export`) over a non-standard module system. You can always transpile to your preferred module system.

clauses.text: Do not use wildcard imports.
clauses.reason: Sample precedence: import/no-namespace retains its inherited/explicit options and severity.

clauses.text: And do not export directly from an import.

clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use dot notation when accessing properties. eslint: [`dot-notation`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/dot-notation)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Always use `const` or `let` to declare variables. Not doing so will result in global variables. We want to avoid polluting the global namespace. Captain Planet warned us of that. eslint: [`no-undef`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-undef) [`prefer-const`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/prefer-const)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use one `const` or `let` declaration per variable or assignment. eslint: [`one-var`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/one-var)

clauses.text: Assign variables where you need them, but place them in a reasonable place.
clauses.reason: A reasonable declaration location is a human judgment.

clauses.text: Don’t chain variable assignments. eslint: [`no-multi-assign`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-multi-assign)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Avoid using unary increments and decrements (`++`, `--`). eslint [`no-plusplus`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-plusplus)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Avoid linebreaks before or after `=` in an assignment. If your assignment violates [`max-len`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/max-len), surround the value in parens. eslint [`operator-linebreak`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/operator-linebreak).
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Disallow unused variables. eslint: [`no-unused-vars`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-unused-vars)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: `var` declarations get hoisted to the top of their closest enclosing function scope, their assignment does not. `const` and `let` declarations are blessed with a new concept called [Temporal Dead Zones (TDZ)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/let#temporal_dead_zone_tdz). It’s important to know why [typeof is no longer safe](https://web.archive.org/web/20200121061528/http://es-discourse.com/t/why-typeof-is-no-longer-safe/15).
clauses.reason: Educational explanation of hoisting and temporal dead zones.

clauses.text: Anonymous function expressions hoist their variable name, but not the function assignment.
clauses.reason: Educational explanation of anonymous function hoisting.

clauses.text: Named function expressions hoist the variable name, not the function name or the function body.
clauses.reason: Educational explanation of named function expression hoisting.

clauses.text: Function declarations hoist their name and the function body.
clauses.reason: Educational explanation of function declaration hoisting.

clauses.text: Use `===` and `!==` over `==` and `!=`. eslint: [`eqeqeq`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/eqeqeq)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Conditional statements such as the `if` statement evaluate their expression using coercion with the `ToBoolean` abstract method and always follow these simple rules:
clauses.reason: Educational explanation of boolean coercion.

clauses.text: Use shortcuts for booleans, but explicit comparisons for strings and numbers.
clauses.reason: Requires semantic types for arbitrary JavaScript expressions; review manually.

clauses.text: For more information see [Truth Equality and JavaScript](https://javascriptweblog.wordpress.com/2011/02/07/truth-equality-and-javascript/#more-2108) by Angus Croll.
clauses.reason: Further-reading reference, not a code requirement.

clauses.text: Use braces to create blocks in `case` and `default` clauses that contain lexical declarations (e.g. `let`, `const`, `function`, and `class`). eslint: [`no-case-declarations`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-case-declarations)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Ternaries should not be nested and generally be single line expressions. eslint: [`no-nested-ternary`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-nested-ternary)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Avoid unneeded ternary statements. eslint: [`no-unneeded-ternary`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-unneeded-ternary)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: When mixing operators, enclose them in parentheses. The only exception is the standard arithmetic operators: `+`, `-`, and `**` since their precedence is broadly understood. We recommend enclosing `/` and `*` in parentheses because their precedence can be ambiguous when they are mixed.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use block statements within control structures, and break up block statements into multiple lines. eslint: [`curly`](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/curly) [`brace-style`](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/brace-style)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: If you’re using multiline blocks with `if` and `else`, put `else` on the same line as your `if` block’s closing brace. eslint: [`brace-style`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/brace-style)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: If an `if` block always executes a `return` statement, the subsequent `else` block is unnecessary. A `return` in an `else if` block following an `if` block that contains a `return` can be separated into multiple `if` blocks. eslint: [`no-else-return`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-else-return)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: In case your control statement (`if`, `while` etc.) gets too long or exceeds the maximum line length, each (grouped) condition could be put into a new line. The logical operator should begin the line.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Don't use selection operators in place of control statements.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use `/** ... */` for multiline comments.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use `//` for single line comments. Place single line comments on a newline above the subject of the comment. Put an empty line before the comment unless it’s on the first line of a block.
clauses.reason: Sample precedence: line-comment-position, lines-around-comment retains its inherited/explicit options and severity.

clauses.text: Start all comments with a space to make it easier to read. eslint: [`spaced-comment`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/spaced-comment)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Prefixing your comments with `FIXME` or `TODO` helps other developers quickly understand if you’re pointing out a problem that needs to be revisited, or if it should be fixed in the current pull-request.
clauses.reason: TODO/FIXME classify work urgency; the author annotation is explicitly optional.

clauses.text: To force right style of comments every eslint config should connect [eslint-plugin-jsdoc](https://github.com/gajus/eslint-plugin-jsdoc). With all recommended rules + `jsdoc/require-file-overview`
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use soft tabs (space character) set to 4 spaces. eslint: [`indent`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/indent)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Place 1 space before the leading brace. eslint: [`space-before-blocks`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/space-before-blocks)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Place 1 space before the opening parenthesis in control statements (`if`, `while` etc.). Place no space between the argument list and the function name in function calls and declarations. eslint: [`keyword-spacing`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/keyword-spacing)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use indentation when making long method chains (more than 2 method chains). Use a leading dot, which

clauses.text: Leave a blank line after blocks and before the next statement.
clauses.reason: Sample precedence: padding-line-between-statements retains its inherited/explicit options and severity.

clauses.text: Do not pad your blocks with blank lines. eslint: [`padded-blocks`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/padded-blocks)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Do not use multiple blank lines to pad your code. eslint: [`no-multiple-empty-lines`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-multiple-empty-lines)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Do not add spaces inside parentheses. eslint: [`space-in-parens`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/space-in-parens)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Do not add spaces inside brackets. eslint: [`array-bracket-spacing`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/array-bracket-spacing)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Add spaces inside curly braces. eslint: [`object-curly-spacing`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/object-curly-spacing)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Avoid having lines of code that are longer than 120 characters (including whitespace). Note: per [above](#strings--line-length), long strings are exempt from this rule, and should not be broken up. eslint: [`max-len`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/max-len)

clauses.text: Require consistent spacing inside an open block token and the next token on the same line. This rule also enforces consistent spacing inside a close block token and previous token on the same line. eslint: [`block-spacing`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/block-spacing)

clauses.text: If for whatever reason you are doing something wild and `parseInt` is your bottleneck and need to use Bitshift for [performance reasons](https://jsperf.com/coercion-vs-casting/3), leave a comment explaining why and what you’re doing.

clauses.text: **Note:** Be careful when using bitshift operations. Numbers are represented as [64-bit values](https://es5.github.io/#x4.3.19), but bitshift operations always return a 32-bit integer ([source](https://es5.github.io/#x11.7)). Bitshift can lead to unexpected behavior for integer values larger than 32 bits. [Discussion](https://github.com/airbnb/javascript/issues/109). Largest signed 32-bit Int is 2,147,483,647:
clauses.reason: Educational warning about bitwise numeric range.

clauses.text: Booleans: eslint: [`no-new-wrappers`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-new-wrappers)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Avoid single letter names. Be descriptive with your naming. eslint: [`id-length`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/id-length)
clauses.reason: Sample precedence: id-length retains its inherited/explicit options and severity.

clauses.text: Use camelCase when naming objects, functions, and instances. eslint: [`camelcase`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/camelcase)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use PascalCase only when naming constructors or classes. eslint: [`new-cap`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/new-cap)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Do not use trailing or leading underscores. eslint: [`no-underscore-dangle`](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-underscore-dangle)
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Don’t save references to `this`. Use arrow functions or [Function#bind](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/bind).
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use PascalCase when you export a constructor / class / singleton / function library / bare object.
clauses.reason: Identifying a singleton or function library requires API-level intent.

clauses.text: Acronyms and initialisms should always be all uppercased, or all lowercased.
clauses.reason: Recognizing domain acronyms requires a project vocabulary.

clauses.text: Use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE when naming constants.
clauses.reason: The guide distinguishes semantic constants from ordinary const bindings without defining a boundary.

clauses.text: Accessor functions for properties are not required.
clauses.reason: Accessor functions are explicitly optional.

clauses.text: Do not use JavaScript getters/setters as they cause unexpected side effects and are harder to test, maintain, and reason about. Instead, if you do make accessor functions, use `getVal()` and `setVal('hello')`.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: If the property/method is a `boolean`, use `isVal()` or `hasVal()`.
clauses.reason: Boolean API intent cannot be inferred reliably for arbitrary JavaScript methods.

clauses.text: It’s okay to create `get()` and `set()` functions, but be consistent.
clauses.reason: Consistency of get/set APIs is a design-review requirement.

clauses.text: Use `Number.isNaN` instead of global `isNaN`.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use `Number.isFinite` instead of global `isFinite`.
clauses.reason: Configured rule enforces the linked syntactic requirement; semantic intent remains reviewable.

clauses.text: Use `PascalCase` enum names and enum properties.
clauses.reason: Enum and member casing is enforced. Singular English names require review; values are unrestricted.

clauses.text: Use `strict: true` in your `tsconfig.json` file.
clauses.reason: Enforced by shared tsconfig settings and compiler integration tests.

clauses.text: Use `"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true` in your `tsconfig.json` file. This is a good practice because it prevents you from accessing elements that don't exist. Read more about it [here](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig#noUncheckedIndexedAccess).
clauses.reason: Enforced by shared tsconfig settings and compiler integration tests.

clauses.text: Use `unknown` type for caught errors.
clauses.reason: Explicit any is rejected; unannotated catches use unknown through strict compiler settings.

ag-compat/no-restricted-syntax.message: for..in loops iterate over the entire prototype chain, which is virtually never what you want. Use Object.{keys,values,entries}, and iterate over the resulting array.
iterators/generators require regenerator-runtime, which is too heavyweight for this guide to allow them. Separately, loops should be avoided in favor of array iterations.
Labels are a form of GOTO; using them makes code confusing and hard to maintain and understand.
`with` is disallowed in strict mode because it makes code impossible to predict and optimize.

patterns.message: Do not import directly from MV2/MV3 implementations. Use the appropriate alias or index file instead.

rules.message: Do not import directly from src/. Use specific submodules like src/utils instead.
